subject: math

entries: A complex number is a point on the Argand diagram: z = 3 + 2i is plotted 3 across the real axis and then 2 up the imaginary axis, and that landing point is the number.
slots.label: A complex number is a point
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Modulus is the distance from the origin: the line from the origin to z is the hypotenuse of the right triangle with legs x and y, so |z| = sqrt(x^2 + y^2).
slots.label: Modulus is the distance
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Argument is the angle; the conjugate mirrors it: arg(z) is the angle of the arrow from the origin, and the conjugate x - iy is the reflection in the real axis, with arg(conjugate of z) = -arg(z).
slots.label: Argument and the conjugate
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Multiplying rotates and stretches: moduli multiply and arguments add, so multiplying by i is a quarter turn, and De Moivre gives arg(z^n) = n arg(z) before wrapping.
slots.label: Multiplying rotates and stretches
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A common mistake: angles wrap around: multiplying the argument can carry it past 180 degrees, so subtract or add 360 degrees until it lands in the principal range -180 to 180 degrees.
slots.label: A common mistake
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A number of the form z = x + iy, where x and y are real numbers and i^2 = -1: x is the real part and y is the imaginary part.
slots.label: Complex number
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The distance of the point z from the origin on the Argand diagram: |z| = sqrt(x^2 + y^2) by Pythagoras.
slots.label: Modulus
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The angle arg(z) that the arrow from the origin to z makes with the positive real axis, measured anticlockwise; it is only defined up to whole turns of 360 degrees.
slots.label: Argument
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The one value of the argument in the principal range -180 to 180 degrees, written Arg(z): every other value differs from it by a whole number of 360-degree turns.
slots.label: Principal argument
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: For z = x + iy, the conjugate is x - iy: the mirror image of z in the real axis, with the same modulus and the negated argument.
slots.label: Conjugate
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The plane used to picture complex numbers: the horizontal axis is the real part and the vertical axis is the imaginary part, so z = x + iy is the point (x, y).
slots.label: Argand diagram
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: JC H2 complex numbers: the Argand diagram
